To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the random order model is a powerful tool that can be used to design optimal online convex optimization algorithms, and that the stability of stochastic gradient descent plays an important role for analyzing such algorithms in this model.

(1) the optimal regret bounds in the random order setting are of the same form as in the i.i.d. case, but with a different dependence on the strong convexity of the objective; (2) the dimension dependence is removed; and (3) the dependence on strong convexity is improved.

(i) the random order model can be used to obtain optimal regret bounds for online learning with strongly convex losses, and that (ii) the optimal regret bound for strongly convex losses is $\tilde{O}\left(1/\sqrt{T}\right)$ for any $T \geq 1$.
